title: Soft Decking on a Tear-Off
description: Soft roof decking shows up after a Houston tear-off. Here is how the bad sheets get marked, priced by the sheet, and replaced before the new shingles go on.
html:
The bid can name the shingle, the underlayment, and the flashing, and still not know the deck. The deck is hidden until the old roof is in the dumpster. Soft plywood or OSB is the line item that surprises people. It should be a line you already understand, not a number invented on the driveway.

What “soft” means under a boot

A stained sheet is not automatically rotten. Water marks the wood and then dries. Soft means the sheet gives underfoot, the veneer has separated, or a screw will not hold. We walk it after the tear-off, mark the sheets that have to go, and photograph them while they are open. A dark ring around an old pipe boot often takes one sheet. A valley that has been wet for years can take a run of them.

You should hear the count before we replace them. Our replacement scopes price decking by the sheet so the morning of the job is arithmetic, not a fresh negotiation. If the job is an insurance claim, those photos are also what a supplement needs. The adjuster who wrote the original scope could not see the deck either. How a Texas roof claim actually goes is the longer version of that sequence.

What we put back

Replacement deck matches the thickness the roof was built with, fastened on the layout, with clips where the edges need them. We do not skim a soft spot with a shingle and hope. We also do not replace every stained sheet to fatten the invoice. If it holds a fastener and does not flex, it stays.

Attic access, when you have it, lets us flag the worst bays before tear-off day. It does not replace the walk on the open deck. On a roof installation, ask any bidder how decking is priced before you sign. We would rather tell you on the inspection. Request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
